column3: NASB renders “having run directly” as “ran a straight course” and adds “had set sail.”
NASB renders “boat” as “ship.”
NASB follows the critical text (“landed”); “was unloading” is rendered “was to unload.”
NASB follows the critical text; “were telling” is rendered “kept telling,” and “to go up to” is “to set foot in.”
NASB follows the critical text; it moves “we said farewell to one another” from v. 6 into this verse and adds “there.”
NASB begins after the greeting moved to v. 5; “their own” is rendered “home again.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB follows the critical text without “those with Paul”; it reads “we departed and came.”
NASB renders “prophesying” as “who were prophetesses.”
NASB follows the critical text without “of us”; “many days” is rendered “some days.”
NASB follows the critical text (“his own”); it reorders the quotation as “the man who owns this belt.” A full-width colon appears in the NASB text.
NASB renders “those of that place” as “the local residents” and “were begging” as “began begging.”
NASB follows the critical text (“Then”).
NASB renders “having said” as “remarking.”
NASB renders “having packed the baggage” as “got ready.”
NASB restructures the verse; “an early disciple” is rendered “a disciple of long standing.”
NASB follows the critical text.
NASB renders “arrived” as “were present.”
NASB renders “was relating” as “began to relate.”
NASB follows the critical text (“God,” “among the Jews”); “myriads” is rendered “thousands.”
NASB renders “apostasy from Moses” as “to forsake Moses.”
NASB follows the critical text without “the multitude must come together”; “What is it?” is rendered “What, then, is to be done?”
Close to the Greek.
NASB follows the critical text; “bear expense” is rendered “pay their expenses,” and “are nothing” is “there is nothing to the things.”

NASB follows the critical text without the Textus Receptus words “that they observe no such thing, except”; “idol-sacrifices” is rendered “meat sacrificed to idols,” and “sexual immorality” is “fornication.”
NASB renders “declaring” as “giving notice” and “fulfillment” as “completion.”
NASB renders “were about to be completed” as “were almost over.”
NASB follows the critical text; “Men Israelites” is rendered “Men of Israel,” and “help” is “come to our aid.” It adds “our.”
NASB renders “having foreseen” as “had previously seen.”
NASB renders “was thrown into commotion” as “was aroused.”
